statement: When bounding a headless `claude -p` subprocess to a read-only toolset, `--allowedTools` alone does NOT restrict the toolset — you must also pass `--disallowedTools` to actually block Bash/Write/Edit/etc; `--allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob"` combined with `--permission-mode dontAsk` still let the model run Bash successfully in a direct empirical test
rationale: Verified by direct test: `claude -p --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob" --permission-mode dontAsk ...` was asked to run `whoami` via Bash and it did, printing the real output. Only adding `--disallowedTools "Bash,Write,Edit,..."` explicitly blocked it (confirmed the model then reported Bash wasn't in its toolset). Any future code trying to sandbox a claude -p call to read-only tools must set both flags, not just allowedTools.
